Well, I became a fitness addict at that point. Couple of years pass, I get into P90X. Did the whole program and was in the best physical shape of my life. Worked out 6 days a week, dated, hung out with friends, went mountain biking. Got a promotion at work with a substantial pay increase. It seemed as if I had reached a pinnacle.

Then in 2011, 2 weeks after completing a grueling mountain biking trail, I suffered a ruptured brain aneurysm and nearly died. I spent 40 days in ICU. I lost every single bit of muscle I had. My calves contracted from being laid up in bed for so long. It took many months of PT to stretch them back out and I still have problems in the morning. Trying to make a long story short even though I was fully insured I was left with over $50K in medical bills. I eventually had to move out of my house into a smaller apartment to save money. Even though I had long term disability insurance coverage the insurance provider refused to pay me. By the time I moved into the apartment I was living on a savings account I had managed to save a good bit of money. A year passed, I appealed the LTD insurance, they still disapproved even with documented brain injury issues. I had to begin to sell off all my personal belongings. I mean everything. A whole house full of furniture, as many clothes as I could. Hell, I just advertised it as a "everything must go" sell and opened my apartment to everyone who read the ad. In the end I was left with my clothes and some sentimental personal stuff. But I was still able to make my car payment.

I sunk into the great depression. My best friend came to visit and brought 4 huge bags of my favorite candy bars. It was with great intentions but the worst thing she could do at that point because in my depression I ate every single one of those candy bars in a week. Within 2 weeks I had gained 10 pounds. Nothing fit anymore and guess what. I didn't have the money to go buy clothes that did fit. The final straw - the culmination of a series of unbelievable events was when my almost brand new car was repossessed because I had not been able to make the payment for 3 months in a row. I now drive an older model Chevy. It's not fancy but it is reliable and paid for. Nobody can take it from me.

I determined I would fix this. I had just beat death and wasn't going to ruin my life by letting my health go to shit by getting fat. I banned junk food from my house. I began walking again every day. It's amazing what exercise does for depression. Try it if you haven't. I lost those 10 pounds and am back to the size I was before that aneurysm burst in my head. I don't have the muscle I had back then because I just don't have the stamina for those kinds of workouts. But I do get out every day and I bike or I walk.

Today it's been just over 5 years since that aneurysm changed my life. I truly reached one of the lowest points in my life. It's been up and down. I moved 4 times in one year. I finally am at home. I'm sharing a home with a family member on an island. My life has gotten exponentially better since those dark days of being broke, being angry, angry at the world. You will get there too. But in the mean time, perhaps just go for a walk?
